title: Dyn-VPP: Video Prediction Policy Optimization for Improved Visual Dynamics
claim: Likelihood-based training of a predictor uses surrogate objectives and suffers credit hacking; reinforcement learning with terminal rewards optimizes the target directly.
layout: Top pipeline row, bottom two panels contrasting prior versus ours, left-to-right
description: The top row shows a robot manipulation pipeline. An instruction ('Pick up the apple') and the current observation image feed a blue Video Prediction Model box that contains a denoising chain x_σI → x_σI-1 → … → x_σ0. The model outputs future observation frames. A 'Visual Dynamics' arrow runs above the chain to a yellow Action Generation Model box, which drives a robot arm that outputs the action. A callout from the video model opens a large blue lower band split by a dashed vertical line. The left panel, '(i) Pretraining & Fine-tuning', uses maximum likelihood via ELBO with an ODE chain and a loss against GT. It has a sad face and red ✗ marks for 'Surrogate Objective' and 'Credit Hacking'. The right panel, '(ii) Post-Training (Ours)', uses an SDE/ODE Euler hybrid sampler with N rollouts and rewards against GT. It has a happy face and green ✓ marks for 'Direct Objective' and 'Credit Assignment'. Emoji faces and check/cross icons draw the eye first.

abstract: Video action models are a promising foundation for Vision–Language–Action (VLA) because they can learn rich visual dynamics directly from video. However, likelihood-oriented training of diffusion predictors emphasizes globally plausible futures and does not guarantee precision-critical visual dynamics needed for manipulation, so small prediction errors can be amplified by downstream policies. We propose Dyn-VPP, a post-training framework that casts multi-step denoising as policy optimization and aligns predicted future latents with expert visual dynamics via verifiable terminal reward, without modifying any architecture. This enables explicit optimization of dynamics signals that are not captured by likelihood-only training. As a result, Dyn-VPP yields more accurate visual dynamics and improves downstream task execution. Experiments across diverse simulated and real-world manipulation settings show improved dynamics consistency and consistently higher task success.
